content.thinking:
I need to plan out the whole scene carefully in one pass since I can't test incrementally. I'm picturing a Genshin-style workbench, about 2.2m wide, 0.8m deep, with a 0.9m tall table and a back shelf rising to 1.6m, decorated with cel-shaded paint, gold filigree, glowing potions, and tassels. Most elements will be plain static parts, reserving joints only for anything that actually needs to move.

I should set up one root joint at the origin so every part has something to attach to, keeping the structure simple without extra hinges for now. I'll lean on cel-shaded paint for large surfaces to keep the flat-color palette under the limit, and build small helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and spheres, plus use a lathe shape for bottle geometry to get that glass-bottle silhouette.

Now I'm laying out the scene: a table at a fixed height and size, with a shelf unit behind it, all centered along the x-axis, and I'm starting to define the table's top slab, trim, and legs.

Legs get lathe-carved feet and stretcher rails, plus a lower shelf stocked with clutter like barrels, sacks, and a crate, while the apron includes three drawers with gold knobs and decals. For the wood texture I'm using a cel-shaded grain pattern with a brownish gradient running along the x-axis. Then I start on the back shelf unit, sizing a back panel positioned behind the table up to roughly 1.8 meters tall.

Above that I'm adding two shelf boards, side posts topped with gold finials, and a crown plank decorated with a moon/sun filigree, plus hanging herb bundles strung from a rod near the top, settling the model's max height around 1.85m. Now I'm laying out the tabletop items starting from the left side, beginning with a stack of books and an open book on a stand.

For the rest of the table I'm placing a tilting balance scale with chained pans and gold weights at center-left, an alembic distillation setup with a glowing flask, burner flame, and curved copper neck leading to a receiving flask plus a mortar and pestle at center, and a potion rack with three tiers of glowing bottles on the right.

I'm also scattering tabletop details—herb bundles, potted plants, a scroll and quill, an hourglass, a glowing crystal cluster, mushrooms—and adding a decorative runner cloth with tassels across the front edge. On the shelves above I'm layering bottle rows, labeled jars, a glowing slime jar, a small crystal, a golden armillary sphere, stacked books, and hanging herb bunches before moving on to textures.

I'm planning a flat rune-circle glyph decal on the floor beneath the workbench, positioned just above ground level so it doesn't clip, and considering adding a circular rug disc under the whole setup, sized to fit without exceeding reasonable width limits.

Simplifying further, I'll just make the rug an elliptical plane with an svg texture painted on top, positioned slightly above a cylinder base for thickness, facing upward toward the back so the drawing reads correctly.

For the Genshin piece, I'm settling on gold filigree colors—a lighter cel gold and darker shade—alongside cream and deep teal fabric tones, using two-tone cel paints that keep texel density low on large flat surfaces so they don't eat into the paint budget.

For the table wood grain, I need higher density given its size, so I'm bumping paintSize to 2048 and keeping the atlas at 4096, while keeping other SVGs modest (rug 512, smaller items 128-256) to avoid forcing the atlas to halve.

For glowing liquids and flames, flat colors should stay well under the 64 limit, with cel shading used elsewhere; for glass bottles, I'm thinking the body itself should be the glowing liquid shape so it reads properly, with a glass shell layered on top instead of opaque glass hiding the contents.

I'm designing the bottle construction: a thin glass rim band at the base, a lighter-tinted glass neck with a cork, and a white highlight stripe swept across the body for a cel-shaded glossy look, then planning a reusable potion helper function that takes position, kind, color, and scale, defining outline profiles like "round" for different flask shapes.

Still writing profile points...

Still designing potion components...

Working out the beam geometry now, tilting it slightly so the pans hang asymmetrically, then computing the endpoints and chain rods connecting to each pan.

Still designing pan shapes and rod placement...

Now I'm planning the table layout, dividing it into zones along x for different apparatus: a potion rack with bottles on one side, the balance scale and mortar in the middle-left, the alembic setup centrally, and books with a candle on the opposite side.

I'm also working out depth placement, keeping flat items like mortars and herb bundles toward the front, with the back shelf unit positioned just behind the table edge, checking clearances so shelf boards and bottle heights don't collide with the shelving above.

For the shelf unit itself, I'm laying out posts with finial spheres, a back panel sized to fit between them, and two shelf boards at specific heights and depths, plus a crown piece at the top with a moon-sun ornament design to cap the structure.

I'm deciding on a decorative gabled crest shape above the panel with a gold trim layer behind a slightly smaller teal wood layer for depth. Given the scope, I'll write the code efficiently using helper loops, aiming for roughly 400 parts while keeping correctness as the priority over maximal detail.

Setting up imports carefully...

Defining the wood and cream color palettes using grain textures with different axis orientations for table top versus legs...

Cork, string, and gem glow colors round out the palette. Now I'm setting up the builder scaffold and helper functions for constructing boxes, handling color types and fill parameters correctly.

Writing geometry helpers...

Still building table geometry...

Still defining leg geometry...

Now I'm adding stretcher rails and a lower shelf between the legs, plus small decorative props like barrels, sacks, and crates to populate the shelf with varied shapes and textures.

Still writing barrel geometry...

I'm adding darker corner slats to the crate and placing a few glowing potion bottles peeking out from the top, overlapping slightly into the hidden interior. Now I'm positioning a teal table runner with a gold border under the alembic, working out its placement and scale across the table front.

Adding tassel details to the runner ends...

Working out book geometry... thinking through a helper that builds covers, spine, and page blocks with rotation offsets computed manually per book orientation.

Still building the book parts...

I'll add four small gold corner boxes near the edges of each cover for accent detail, plus a gold star/sun emblem decal on the cover. Then I'm positioning a stack of three lying books with slight varied yaws on top of the stack, and planning a candle placed above them.

For the stack height, I'm calculating each book's center y-position based on cumulative thicknesses, then adding a brass candlestick with a lathe-shaped base, a cream wax cylinder candle, and a glowing orange cone flame on top. I'm also planning an open book on a simple X-frame wooden stand nearby, with two tilted page halves forming a V-shape to suggest open pages.

Working out rotation math...

So left half tilts -6°, right half +6°, with cover plates underneath and text decals placed in the rotated local frame of each half. I'm also planning a thin ribbon bookmark hanging down from between the pages to the table.

Next I'm adding a rolled parchment scroll lying near the front, with spiral end caps and a tied red ribbon, plus an inkwell with a quill resting against it — the quill's feather made from an extruded leaf-shaped outline tapering to a sharp tip.

Now I'm working out the quill's direction vector and feather thickness, then moving on to an alembic setup with a tripod brazier made of angled gold legs supporting a ring.

Adding burner and flask geometry...

Still computing neck and dome dimensions, then sketching a condenser pipe as a curved sweep from the dome tip down toward a receiving flask.

Finishing the pipe curve so it ends right at the receiver neck top, with a thin copper tube radius and gold bands placed along the sweep at intervals.

I'll add a small droplet sphere at the pipe's end and skip rising bubbles since they'd be hidden inside. For the receiver stand, I'll use a brass torus as a cork ring base. Then I'm moving to the mortar and pestle, lathing the mortar's stone bowl profile from base up the outer wall, across the rim, and down into the bowl interior.

I'm checking the profile points don't self-intersect along the rim curve, then adding a tilted pestle rod as a tapered capsule shape from the bowl toward an upper offset point, plus a thin green disc to represent herb powder sitting inside the bowl.

Now I'm designing a three-tier potion rack as a stair-stepped stand, building each tier as a box with increasing height and depth offset further back in z, positioning them so the tops align with the step pattern.

Adding gold trim and arranging rows of 4 bottles per tier, spacing them along x, with the back row taller than the front. I'm defining an elemental color palette for the bottle glows—cyan, red, purple, green, blue, ice, and gold—cycling through them as I place each bottle.

Checking vertical clearances, I realize the tier-3 bottles would collide with the lower shelf board at the current heights, so I need to raise the shelf positions to give enough headroom for the tallest bottles.

Let me finalize: posts up to 1.88, top beam at 1.88, finials at 1.95, with crest work pushing total height to about 2.1m, which is reasonable for a tall workbench shelf unit. Now I'm working out the hanging herb rail, placing a rod near the shelf front so bunches dangle down without colliding with items on the lower shelf board.

Actually I'll place just 4 bunches at the sides, x=±0.95 and ±0.78, and add a single glowing lantern hanging on a chain at center, with its body positioned in front of the shelf. For the bunches themselves, I'm building each as a tied string with herb-sprig card textures made of stems and leaves...

For the texture variety, I'm setting up three herb types—green sprigs, lavender, and chili-red—with randomized spin and position per card so bunches don't look uniform. I also realize I need to account for the drawing orientation: since the card is viewed from downstream, the root edge attaches at the top, meaning the stem of each sprig drawing needs to sit at the bottom of its SVG so it reads correctly when hung.

For potted plants like the fern, I'm generating standing card frames around a circle, tilting each outward from vertical so the leaves splay naturally from the pot, using a broad-leaf texture and enabling cross-billboarding for volume.

For the glowing sprout, I'm sweeping green stems with catmull curves and topping them with ring-shaped petal cones that glow cyan, like an invented luminous bell flower for that Genshin aesthetic.

For the mushroom cluster, I'm building cream cylindrical stalks with hemisphere caps (partial sphere geometry) and painting red-and-white spotted textures onto them, placing the group near the fern. Now I'm starting on a glowing crystal cluster using elongated octahedra for the shelf display.

I'm placing an hourglass with glass cones holding glowing gold sand, brass end plates, and connecting rods on shelf one, alongside an armillary sphere made of rotated gold torus rings around a glowing core on shelf two. For shelf one's left section, I'm arranging a row of standing books with gold decorative bands across their spines facing outward.

Next to the books I'm adding a small title plate and tilting the last book slightly for a leaning effect, then placing glowing glass jars further along the shelf—dark teal jar bodies with glowing green liquid inside, brass lids, and label cards decorated with herb illustrations on their fronts.

Adding a small plant and pouch on top, then designing a decorative back panel between shelves—a gold diamond lattice pattern over deep teal as a wallpaper-style decal, sized to fit the panel dimensions and positioned just in front of the panel surface.

Now I'm building the crest ornament at the top: a gold sun disc surrounded by a ring of twelve small cones arranged radially, plus flourish shapes extruded as plaque outlines for the base decoration... Writing extrude outline code...

Now I'm adding a hanging lantern centerpiece: gold corner posts, cone roof, and a glowing amber core box, suspended by chain rods from the top beam. I'm positioning it to sit in front of the upper shelf items without clipping, thinking through bracket and arm placement to hang it properly from the beam.

Instead I'm reworking the support structure—hanging the lantern from a crossbar rod spanning between two posts, with the posts themselves repositioned to rest on the table top rather than the floor, figuring out proper depth and spacing so nothing overlaps the shelves or table edges.

Rods extend from the posts forward to z=0 with a cross rod connecting them at y=1.85, positioned well in front of the shelf so hanging items clear the tabletop pieces like the potion rack and lantern without colliding.

I'm working through placement math for the lantern and alembic to avoid overlap - checking alembic pipe reach versus lantern x-position, settling on lantern center around x=0.7, y=1.62, clearing the alembic's top pipe at roughly 1.45. Then I'm spacing out the hanging bunches along x from -0.9 to 0.0 with drop lengths around 0.25, keeping their bottoms above the rack bottles below.

Next I'm checking overall model dimensions - table 2.2 wide, rug 2.7 - which seems fine, then moving to think about label textures for the bottles, planning small SVG labels with herb/drop symbols in 2-3 color variants, plus potion tags hung on neck strings.

Building out the full texture atlas list now...

Still writing rug SVG... Then I'll build a star-polygon helper function for the compass rune and ring dots via loops, sized at 768x561 to match the rug's aspect ratio. For the page texture, I'm planning grey-brown ruled lines, a drop cap, and a small leaf illustration on a transparent background.

I'm defining a potion profile system with a Kind type (round/tall/cone/gourd) mapping to body outline point arrays, using flat cel-shaded colors for glass, liquids, and flames rather than full toon shading since the painted look already bakes in the shading.

Still writing profile coordinates...

Adding neck, lip, and cork geometry...

Placing the flat highlight ellipsoid at the viewer-left front of the body, then working out the tag position near the neck front, checking its height and depth against the shoulder radius so it sits just outside the body without clipping.

I'm counting parts per potion (lathe body, neck, lip, cork, ring, highlight, tag = 7, totaling 175 across 25 potions), planning three label textures as rounded cream cards with gold borders and symbols, and sketching glow cones for flames. For floor decor I'm adding a small dark iron cauldron on the rug near the table's front-right corner, giving it a bubbling glow effect.

Still writing cauldron profile...

Adding dark iron legs, a gold rim torus, handles, and a ladle for the cauldron, then checking its position against the table so it doesn't overlap. I'm considering adding small glowing ember logs or flame cones beneath the cauldron for a lit-fire effect, keeping it simple with a few fire cones instead of a full log pile.

Now I'm setting rotation parameters for horizontal cylinders and preparing to write the full TypeScript file, being careful with strict typing for rotation vectors and a reusable glow helper for parts. Writing scene code...

Still defining paint and shape helpers...

Now I'm building the table geometry, setting the tabletop slab with a wood finish and adding thin gold inlay strips along its front, back, and side edges for decorative trim.

I'm adding the apron panels beneath the tabletop around all four sides, then laying out three evenly spaced drawer fronts with gold inlay framing each one.

Now I'm adding drawer hardware: ball knobs with backplates and small keyhole details, plus placing the lathed legs at each corner using a turned profile for the leg shape.

Moving on to the stretchers connecting the legs for structural support.

Then I'm populating the lower shelf with a barrel-generating function and scattering items on top—barrels of varying sizes, sacks, and a crate—to furnish the storage space.

I'm also deciding whether to add a tied herb bundle on the table, considering rod-and-card approaches for stems and leaves, and settling on placing it standing in a ceramic jug with a sprouting lavender sprig made from tilted frames and textured cards.

Now I'm laying out precise table coordinates to avoid collisions: the potion rack at x=-0.78 with tiered shelves, the lavender jug at (-0.95, 0.4), the mortar at (-0.62, 0.33), mushrooms at (-0.4, 0.42), and the balance scale base around (-0.3, 0.0), while still placing the fern pot, glow flower pot, and book stacks nearby.

Now I'm placing the runner cloth under the alembic and receiver, centering it around x=0.25 with tassels along the front edge, then positioning the book stack and open book nearby, checking their widths don't overlap with the receiver.

Next I'm figuring out the candle on the book stack, the scroll lying along the front edge, and the inkwell with quill near the open book's edge, making sure they all fit without colliding. I'm also placing the fern pot and glow flower pot on the opposite side from the mushrooms, spacing them so each item has its own breathing room.

Then I'm positioning extra items further back: a small flower pot beyond the stack, two tall potion bottles near the back edge, and a crystal cluster nearby, checking that everything clears the shelf height above. Finally I'm working out the balance scale's placement, confirming its pillar and beam height stay just under the shelf overhead.

Writing scale geometry...

Each pan hangs from three chain rods connecting to rim points, with the lower pan holding glowing crystals/herbs and the higher pan holding small brass counterweights (cylinders topped with tiny balls) to sell the physical balance illusion.

Now I'm laying out the rack's tiers, adding thin gold trim strips along each shelf front, then placing rows of bottles (cone, round, tall shapes) across three tiers, checking that bottle heights plus cork clearance stay within the shelf bounds so nothing clips the frame above.

Checking shelf clearances against board positions confirms items under .19 fit on shelf 2. For potions, I need to scale down the tall/round/cone variants to around s=.6-.8 so their combined body, neck, and cork heights stay under the limit—working out that tall needs s≈.6, round s≈.75, cone s≈.8 to hit .18-.24 range. Rack bottles at .85 scale give a row-2 top height around 1.345, which I'm checking against the shelf constraints.

For the alembic, its top lands at 1.42 with no shelf conflict. Now I'm laying out the lower shelf contents: a row of five standing books with varying widths/heights, gold bands, title plates, and a mix of wine/deep/teal/purple/green colors with the last one leaning, followed by two glowing jars placed further along.

Still building jar geometry... now moving to the hourglass: base plates, thin rods, and two opposing cones meeting at the middle to form the glass bulbs with glowing gold sand inside.

Next I'll add scene 4 with a crystal cluster made of tilted octahedrons glowing violet/blue on a stone base, then scene 5 with a round carboy sphere since a tall potion shape felt too stretched.

Adding the neck, cork, and a couple smaller potions nearby, then moving to the upper shelf layout: an armillary sphere at center made from a lathed gold base, stand, and tilted torus rings arranged at different rotation angles to form the classic sphere look.

Filling out the shelf with a glowing core ball and small satellite, then a row of six small bottles with tags on the left and stacked books plus a potted glow flower on the right. For the frame, I'm placing finials, gold collars on the posts, and setting the top beam and panel dimensions to close out the bookshelf structure.

Still working out post and beam coordinates...

Still working out herb bunch placement...

Still placing lantern geometry...

I'm adding corner posts and checking vertical clearance between the lantern's tassel and the candle flame stack—both fit without overlap. Then I'm verifying the cauldron's floor position sits within the rug's elliptical boundary by checking the normalized distance equation, confirming it's comfortably inside at radius .3.

Now I'm defining the rug geometry—a scaled cylinder with specific radii and center offset—and designing the SVG border pattern using a matching elliptical viewBox ratio, with the ground plane oriented upward and positioned just above the cylinder's top surface to avoid z-fighting.

Writing SVG rug pattern...

Now I'm designing the emblem, label, and tassel SVGs: a gold ring-and-star emblem for the book cover, rounded label shapes with drop/leaf/star symbols sized for stroke clarity, and a tassel with the knot positioned at the bottom so strands fan upward toward the hanging point.

I'm also sketching the potted plant leaf shape rooted at the base for standing cards, and planning the glow flower and mushroom cap shapes.

For the scroll object, I'm building a cylinder for the rolled portion with painted texture, adding spiral end caps, a tied ribbon torus, and a flat unrolled sheet using a textured plane for the ink lines.

Now I'm shaping a lathed brass candle holder profile, checking that the outline stays monotone, then adding wax drip details and a flame made of layered glowing cones for the inner and outer glow. I'm moving on to lathe a terracotta plant pot shape next.

Still writing pot geometry...

Now I'm setting up a glow-flower pot with stems built from catmull-rom sweep curves branching upward from the pot center.

Adding cone-shaped glowing petals arranged in a radial ring around each flower head, plus leaf cards near the stem base, and fern pot cards leaning outward with a custom flow direction function.

I'm setting up a single deterministic rng instance to drive card placement counts, then moving on to building the ceramic jug with a lathe profile and gold band accent.

I'm reusing a generic sprigs helper for the hanging herb cards, skipping extras like skulls or hanging keys but considering drawer tags. With a rough part count around 450 total, I'm moving on to write the concrete TypeScript code, keeping part options spreading compatible with scale and other properties.

Writing rotation helpers for lying books...

Adding gold corner accents...and an emblem plane facing outward with white base color so the texture shows its true colors. Pages remain visible at the edges. Now I'm starting a standBook helper function to place upright books on a shelf, handling position, height, depth, cover material, and lean angle.

I'll skip the leaning rotation complexity and just vary heights for the tilted book instead, keeping other details simple. Now I'm organizing the potion label textures into an array and planning to write all the code in one pass, keeping track of which imports and helper types I need.

Writing star and diamond SVG helpers for the rug pattern...

Still writing the rug SVG...

I'm planning the overall build order: define elemental color palette, textures, and helper functions first, then assemble the cauldron, potion rack, and bottles using those helpers.

Writing potion-generator function...

Checking that the highlight sphere position stays near the surface across the round, tall, and cone bottle shapes, verifying the geometry math for each radius profile so the reflective dot doesn't poke outside the glass incorrectly.

Lighting looks fine. Moving to the barrel lathe profile with hoops, then noting potion placement for crate bottles. Now I'm writing the final file, checking types for lathe options, glow parts, and card mesh arrays, plus importing frame helpers for card orientation. I'm adding gold torus rings along the sword using the along callback...

Now writing a sprig generation function that distributes leaves or decorations around a point with configurable size, lean, bend, and spread angles.

Still writing bunch helper...

I'm checking frame orientation with flow flattened onto the plane perpendicular to the axis, then moving on to assemble the final code, double-checking unused imports like grain, mottle, spots, and INK before wrapping up with the root return.

Writing crest outline arrays, being careful with the OutlinePoint tuple typing when destructuring and scaling...

Working out the crest positioning on the gold beam, layering a gold outline and a teal outline at slightly offset depths and thicknesses so they sit visibly on top of each other at the panel back.

Now I'm placing a sun disc at the top of the crest with radiating cone-shaped rays arranged in a circle around it, plus a small glowing gem at the center, and setting the crest's overall height to extend about a quarter unit above the base.

I'm moving on to writing out the full scene: adding glowing lantern parts with a warm gold color, double-checking helper function signatures for paints and scaling, and sketching a dark glass ink well using a lathe shape.
